test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 31 May 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate option fill in the blank.**

I have been studying this course _______ two years now.
solution:
The correct answer is '**for**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate preposition for the given blank is '**for**'.
 
• The word '**for**' is used to show a period of time, in the **past, present, or future.**
 
• The given sentence is in the present **perfect continuous tense.**
 
 
• ***​**Example: I have been reading War and Peace for a month now. *
 
 The word '**since**' is used to refer to a time (an action that began in the past and is still continuing). It is used as a preposition.
 
• So, '**for**' should be used here.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *I have been studying this course **for** two years now.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• **Through **- Incorrect here because "**through**" indicates movement within a time period, e.g., "through the night," but not for indicating a duration of time.
 
• **Since **- Incorrect because "**since**" specifies the starting point of an action or event, e.g., "since 2022," not a duration.
 
• **Almost **- Incorrect because "**almost**" implies an approximation but does not specify the exact time frame, e.g., "almost two years."
